topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The opening framing welcomes students, outlines the lecture series structure and multidisciplinary audience, and introduces the key learning objectives before substantive teaching begins.

topics.label: Biological basis of cancer and tissue organization
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cumulative genetic and epigenetic alterations disrupt developmental differentiation programs and tissue architecture, and discuss the laboratory models used to study these cellular properties.

topics.label: Pathology and progression of invasion and metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how tumors progress from contained, benign precursor lesions to locally invasive and metastatic malignancies, highlighting histological markers such as basement membrane penetration.

topics.label: Tumor classification, nomenclature, and pathophysiological effects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address the diagnostic terminology used to classify neoplasms and the physical and physiological mechanisms by which benign and malignant growths cause patient morbidity and mortality.

topics.label: Cancer epidemiology and comparative oncology across species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics analyze patterns of cancer incidence and organ distribution across human populations, domestic animals, and diverse multicellular organisms.

topics.label: Clinical screening and early detection of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the clinical rationale, diagnostic methods, and tissue-specific challenges of screening programs aimed at catching pre-malignant lesions and early-stage tumors.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and practical preview
topics.groupedBecause: The closing framing reiterates the core learning outcomes, provides directions for revision and upcoming practical sessions, and dismisses the lecture.
